newsitem.title: USA: Congress approves special coins for baseball great.
newsitem.headline: Congress approves special coins for baseball great.

text.p: The House approved a bill Friday authorizing minting of commemorative coins honoring Americans from George Washington to baseball great Jackie Robinson.
The bill, which was sent to the president for signature, also included measures aimed at ensuring that the government did not lose money on coin programs.

In addition to honoring the first U.S. president and the first black baseball player in the Major Leagues, the bill authorized coins for Dolley Madison, wife of the fourth president, Crispus Attucks and other black American Revolutionary War patriots, President Franklin Roosevelt, Yellowstone National Park and the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial in Washington.
The bill would establish a fund for maintenance of the memorial and raise money for the Jackie Robinson Foundation to help needy students.
Under the bill, the new series would start in 1997 with the Roosevelt and Jackie Robinson coins, which would be issued for one year beginning May 15 and July 1.
